title: Automated data eraser, auditable checkpoints, and customer notice flow
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Build an end-to-end automated Right-To-Be-Forgotten (RTBF) workflow that: schedules and executes data deletion across residency zones, emits immutable audit checkpoints for verification, and triggers configurable customer notifications once deletion evidence is available. This ticket covers the PM scope: UX for scheduling and notices, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and cross-team coordination.

Motivation and goals:
- Customers operating under GDPR/CCPA require demonstrable, auditable deletion and proof-of-deletion artifacts tied to a single request ID.
- Existing manual purge flows are error-prone and lack linked evidence for legal reviews; we need automation that scales with Dedicated and Private customers.
- Deliverables: a scheduler + orchestrator contract, an auditable checkpoint format (signed snapshot), a customer-facing notice flow template, and a verification dashboard for SRE/Compliance.

Scope (what's in/out):
In scope:
- Orchestration of delete requests across residency-aware storage (EU/US/APAC) with configurable retention overrides and TTLs.
- Generation of an immutable checkpoint record per purge with metadata: request_id, effected_data_scopes, residency_zone, timestamp, status per system, verification_hash, and operator_signatures.
- Customer notice templates and webhooks for success/failure with links to downloadable evidence bundles.
- Backend APIs for initiating purges and querying evidence status.

Out of scope (for this ticket):
- Deep forensic recovery tools, archival recovery.
- Legal sign-off language for non-EU jurisdictions (handled by Legal as a follow-up).

Acceptance criteria (must have):
1) A new REST endpoint POST /v1/compliance/deletions that accepts request payloads with customer_id, scope selectors, residency constraint, and desired notification channel.
2) Each deletion request produces an immutable checkpoint record (signed by a service key) that is stored in the compliance ledger and accessible via GET /v1/compliance/evidence/{request_id}.
3) For multi-system deletes, checkpoint lists per-system statuses and a final aggregated status (Succeeded/PartiallySucceeded/Failed).
4) Customer is notified when final status is reached; notification includes secure link to the evidence bundle (S3 presigned or internal transfer).
5) Deletion runs honor residency constraints (EU-only data not leaving EU regions) and log the effective locations used.
6) End-to-end smoke tests and an integration test harness that can be run by SRE and Compliance.

Technical approach (high level):
- Scheduler: a durable message-driven scheduler (ENG to implement) will accept requests and push per-system sub-tasks with a request_id. The scheduler supports retries and backoff.
- Checkpoint format: JSON-LD style record that is checksumed and signed with the platform signing key. Includes fields for human-readable summary and per-system digests.
- Evidence bundles: when a request completes, the compliance ledger will create a zipped bundle with logs, per-system receipts, and the signed checkpoint. Bundles will be retained for configurable retention windows for audit.
- Verification: a lightweight verification service will validate signatures, checksums, and per-system receipts; it will provide a boolean verification flag and a verification_log.

Trade-offs considered and decisions made:
- Signed checkpoints vs. WORM storage: decided to implement signed checkpoints plus append-only ledger entries to balance cost and verification guarantees (WORM would be heavier for hosted tenants).
- Synchronous vs. asynchronous deletion: chosen asynchronous orchestration to avoid long API timeouts and reduce coupling across systems.
- Evidence bundle delivery: support both presigned download links for hosted customers and internal push for Private deployments to respect air-gapped constraints.

Progress and workplan (milestones):
- 2026-03-10: PRD drafted and initial alignment with ENG/SRE/Legal. (this ticket created)
- 2026-03-12: Design review with Security & Compliance — feedback captured on signing keys and key rotation.
- 2026-03-18: Engineering spike for scheduler (ENG-2142) planned; API contract stub created.
- 2026-03-24: Audit checkpoint schema v1 finalized; sample evidence bundle generated for review.
- 2026-03-30: End-to-end QA harness ready for internal testing.
- 2026-04-07: Target release to staging (platform-2026.03).

Open risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Key management for signing checkpoints may require HSM/KMS integration for Private customers.
  Mitigation: Engage Security to scope HSM/KMS integration; if high-friction, fall back to tenant-managed encryption keys and store signatures under platform KMS.
- Risk: Cross-region delete coordination complexity could increase completion times and user-facing latency.
  Mitigation: Provide progress webhooks so customers see incremental progress and implement per-system timeouts with clear FinalStatus semantics.
- Risk: Legal/regulatory nuances per country.
  Mitigation: Provide extensible notice templates and let Legal sign standard templates in follow-up ticket.

QA and verification plan:
- Unit tests for checkpoint schema and signature verification.
- Integration test harness simulating multi-region deletes (ENG-2142 test matrix).
- Manual acceptance: Compliance team will run a set of 10 canned RTBF requests and verify evidence bundles and dashboard entries.
- Load testing: ensure scheduler scales to 200 concurrent deletion requests per minute in Dedicated clusters.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- Metric: time_to_final_status (p50/p95/p99) by residency. Target p95 < 5 minutes for single-system deletes; p99 < 30 minutes for cross-region complex deletes.
- Metric: evidence_bundle_generation_failures (target < 0.1%).
- Dashboard: new Compliance -> Purges page in Console showing live statuses, throughput, and evidence download links.

Rollout and migration notes:
- Beta: enable for a small set of tenants (opt-in flag) in staging. Collect evidence artifacts and iterate on bundle contents.
- Migration: for existing manual purges, provide a migration utility to attach existing receipts to new checkpoint records.
